item.title: Simple finite-dimensional binary Lie superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.30386v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every complex finite-dimensional simple binary Lie superalgebra with non-zero odd part is either a simple Lie superalgebra, and hence is one of the superalgebras of Kac's list, or the two-dimensional non-Lie superalgebra $B_2$. This confirms the Grishkov--Shestakov conjecture and, together with the theorems of Grishkov and Filippov on simple binary Lie algebras, gives the answer to Shestakov's question from the Dniester Notebook (Problem 3.100(d)) over the field of complex numbers.
item.dc:creator: Hani Abdelwahab, Ivan Kaygorodov

item.title: Classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebras on solvable Lie conformal algebras of rank two
item.description: arXiv:2610.30471v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we give a complete classification of compatible left-symmetric conformal algebra structures on solvable Lie conformal algebras which are free of rank two as $\mathbb{C}[\partial]$-modules up to isomorphism. We obtain ten mutually non-isomorphic normal-form types and determine the precise equivalence relations among the parameters within each family. Moreover, we also characterize the Novikov conformal algebras among the classified left-symmetric conformal algebras, thereby obtaining a complete classification of compatible Novikov conformal algebra structures in the same setting.
item.dc:creator: Yuanmeng Zhai, Yanyong Hong

item.title: A parametrization of nonassociative Petit algebras $K[t;\sigma]/K[t:\sigma](t^m-a)$ up to equivalence
item.description: arXiv:2610.30921v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $K/F$ be a cyclic Galois field extension of degree $n$ with $\mathrm{Gal}(K/F)=\langle\sigma\rangle$. The nonassociative Petit algebras $K[t;\sigma]/K[t;\sigma](t^m-a)$ have recently emerged as important tools in coding theory and cryptography, where the applications only require distinct algebras up to isomorphism. Algebras that are isomorphic via a monomial isomorphism of degree one are called equivalent. We present a novel and precise parametrization of the $F$-equivalence classes of these algebras in the key case that $F$ contains a primitive $n$th root of unity and $n\mid m$. We evaluate the parametrization explicitly when $F$ is a nonarchimedean local field, which has applications to the number field case recently used to construct a nonassociative variant of Learning with Errors.
item.dc:creator: Monica Nevins, Susanne Pumpluen

item.title: Degenerations of Jordan algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.31179v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We describe all degenerations of complex $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras and of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras. The proofs do not use other papers on degenerations, and all degenerations and non-degenerations were formally verified in the proof assistant Lean~4. The graph of primary degenerations of $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras has $73$ vertices and $160$ edges. The variety of $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras is stratified into $63$ normal forms, five of which are one- or two-parameter families; together with two special members of a family this gives $65$ objects, and the graph of primary degenerations has $154$ edges. In particular, we describe all irreducible components of the corresponding varieties: the variety of $4$-dimensional Jordan algebras has $10$ irreducible components, and the variety of $5$-dimensional nilpotent Jordan algebras has dimension $22$ and $5$ irreducible components.
item.dc:creator: Victor Bovdi, Ivan Kaygorodov, Yury Popov, Azamat Saydaliyev, Yury Volkov

item.title: From Quaternions to Pentarnions I: Algebra, geometry, and a spin model
item.description: arXiv:2610.31485v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce a family of five-dimensional non-flexible quadratic real algebras $\{\mathcal A_\gamma\}_{0\leq\gamma\leq1}$ with canonical basis $1,i,j,k,\ell$, in which $\gamma$ changes the multiplication but not their norm, and study how this change affects geometry and dynamics. The algebras are pairwise non-isomorphic, $\mathcal A_0$ contains Hamilton's quaternion algebra, and $\mathcal A_1$ is the Pentarnion algebra. The alternating part of the trilinear form $\langle u\times_\gamma v,w\rangle$ induced by the multiplication of $\mathcal{A}_\gamma$ defines a three-dimensional subspace $H_\gamma\subset\operatorname{span}_{\mathbb R}\{i,j,k,\ell\}$, tilted by the angle $\arctan(\gamma/\sqrt3)$, whose rotation group $G_\gamma\cong\mathrm{SO}(3)$ contains the automorphism group of $\mathcal A_\gamma$. For $\gamma_1\ne\gamma_2$ the groups $G_{\gamma_1}$ and $G_{\gamma_2}$ generate $\mathrm{SO}(V)\cong\mathrm{SO}(4)$. For the six ways of ordering and bracketing the product of $i,p,p$ in $\mathcal A_\gamma$, two map the unit circle in ${\rm span}\{j,k\}$ to a point and, for $\gamma>0$, four map it to ellipses. As an application, we derive a Hamiltonian model of a classical spin on $H_\gamma$ whose multiplication-induced quadratic energy is isotropic for $\gamma=0$ and anisotropic for $\gamma>0$. It conserves spin length and, for fixed $\gamma$, energy, and satisfies an exact work identity when $\gamma$ varies in time. Numerical experiments with periodically varying $\gamma$ indicate both regular and irregular spin dynamics.
item.dc:creator: Alireza Poshtkohi, Susanne Pumpluen

item.title: Bipartite solutions of the set-theoretic Yang--Baxer equation
item.description: arXiv:2610.30845v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce a new class of unitary set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions, called \emph{bipartite} solutions. This class, which is purely combinatorial in nature, forms a full subcategory of $\mathcal{LYB}$, the category of Lyubashenko type solutions of Agore, Chirvasitu and the author, and is particularly amenable to explicit classification results. We give an intrinsic necessary and sufficient condition for a solution of the Yang--Baxter equation to be isomorphic to a bipartite solution, we settle the isomorphism problem within this class and, as an application, we determine their automorphism groups. If $X$ is a finite set with $|X| = n$, the number of isomorphism classes of bipartite solutions on $X$ is $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1 + \sum_{m=2}^{n} \bigl( o(m, n-m) - 1 \bigr)$, where $o(m, k)$ denotes the number of orbits of the symmetric group $S_m$ acting by conjugation on the $k$-element multisets of elements of $S_m$. The paper also offers a comparative study: for small $|X| = n$ we count, up to isomorphism, all set-theoretic Yang--Baxter solutions on $X$, together with five distinguished families of solutions. Throughout the range we were able to compute, the class $\mathcal{LYB}$ accounts for a large share of all bijective and of all non-degenerate solutions, strikingly close to the total.
item.dc:creator: Gigel Militaru

item.title: Sum-rank analogues of Reed--Muller codes over Abelian Galois extensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.31358v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb L/\mathbb K$ be a finite Abelian Galois extension with a fixed decomposition $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb L/\mathbb K)=\langle\sigma_1\rangle\times\cdots\times\langle\sigma_m\rangle$. We show that the quotient of the multivariate skew polynomial ring $\mathbb L[x_1,\ldots,x_m;\sigma_1,\ldots,\sigma_m]$ by suitable central polynomials $H_1(x_1),\ldots,H_m(x_m)$ is isomorphic to a product of $t$ copies of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbb K}(\mathbb L)$, so that one skew polynomial represents all blocks of a sum-rank metric space. The sum-rank weight of an element equals the rank of an associated Dickson matrix and of a generalized Moore matrix. Using this, we define sum-rank Reed--Muller-type codes and show that their dimension and minimum distance are given by the formulas for affine Cartesian codes with side lengths $\mathrm{deg}\,H_1,\ldots,\mathrm{deg}\,H_m$; the same holds for codes supported on lower sets. The family contains as special cases linearized Reed--Solomon codes, Gabidulin codes, rank-metric Reed--Muller codes, and affine Cartesian codes. Over finite fields, every linearized Reed--Muller code of Berardini and Caruso is, after a monomial change of variables, a monomial code in our framework. This gives the dimension of all these codes, and their exact minimum distance in every degree whenever the support is a lower set.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Neri, Giuseppe Zampella

item.title: Properties of theories whose algebras are free
item.description: arXiv:2610.31599v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: A hard theorem of Givant classifies the finitary algebraic theories for which every algebra is free. From it, one easily deduces that all such theories are minimal (adding any further equations makes them trivial) and have a well-defined notion of dimension (free algebras on sets of different cardinality are never isomorphic). We prove both these properties directly, without the aid of Givant's theorem.
item.dc:creator: Tom Leinster, Maia Woolf

item.title: $\delta$-Superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras
item.description: arXiv:1106.2680v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the paper, a complete description of the $\delta$-derivations and the $\delta$-superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p\neq2$ is given. In particular, new examples of nontrivial $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and odd $\frac{1}{2}$-superderivations are given that are not operators of right multiplication by an element of the superalgebra.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: I. Kaygorodov, $\delta$-Superderivations of semisimple finite-dimensional Jordan superalgebras, Math. Notes 91 (2012), no. 2, 187-197
item.dc:creator: Ivan Kaygorodov

item.title: On conservative algebras of 2-dimensional Algebras
item.description: arXiv:2503.15687v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1990 Kantor introduced the conservative algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ of all algebras (i.e. bilinear maps) on the $n$-dimensional vector space. In case $n >1$ the algebra $\mathcal{W}(n)$ does not belong to well known classes of algebras (such as associative, Lie, Jordan, Leibniz algebras). We describe $\frac{1}{2}$derivations, local (resp. $2$-local) $\frac{1}{2}$-derivations and biderivations of $\mathcal{W}(2)$. We also study similar problems for the algebra $\mathcal{W}_2$ of all commutative algebras on the two-dimensional vector space and the algebra $\mathcal{S}_2$ of all commutative algebras with trace zero multiplication on the two-dimensional space.
item.dc:creator: Hassan Oubba

item.title: Hilbert's Basis Theorem for generalized nonassociative Ore extensions
item.description: arXiv:2512.02597v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a broader class of nonassociative Ore extensions that unifies and generalizes several earlier constructions, taking subadditivity of polynomial degree under multiplication as a guiding principle. We prove generalizations of Hilbert's Basis Theorem for this class, showing that left and right Noetherianity follow from corresponding degree-reduction properties. Applications include flipped nonassociative Ore extensions, mutations, cochain twists, and depolarizations of Poisson Ore extensions.
item.dc:creator: Per B\"ack, Masood Aryapoor

item.title: Three-periodic helices on elliptic curves and their associated regular algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.21900v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ denote an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero and let $X$ denote a smooth elliptic curve over $k$. Given a three-periodic elliptic helix $\underline{\mathcal{E}}$ of vector bundles over $X$ with endomorphism $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ and quadratic cover $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$, we prove that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is the quotient of $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ by a degree three family of normal elements, generalizing a result of the authors to the case in which $\operatorname{dim }(\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}})_{i, i+1}$ isn't a constant function of $i$. We then show that $\operatorname{End} \underline{\mathcal{E}}$ is noetherian if and only if it has polynomial growth, and in this case, the ranks of any three consecutive bundles in the helix are a Markov triple. Furthermore, in this case $\mathbb{S}^{nc}(\underline{\mathcal{E}})$ is a noetherian GK-three $\mathbb{Z}$-algebra which is ${\sf Proj }$-equivalent to an elliptic algebra. We conclude the paper by constructing several new families of elliptic helices with exponential growth.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Chan, Adam Nyman

item.title: Fixed-point-free automorphisms of solvable Lie algebras
item.description: arXiv:2604.27916v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we investigate the existence of fixed-point-free automorphisms for finite-dimensional Lie algebras. By a result of Jacobson, a Lie algebra admitting a fixed-point-free automorphism is solvable. We prove that such a Lie algebra must be even strongly unimodular. We find a necessary and sufficient criterion such that a complex almost abelian Lie algebra admits a fixed-point-free automorphism. For complex filiform Lie algebras we show that the existence of a fixed-point-free automorphism is equivalent to not being characteristically nilpotent.
item.dc:creator: Dietrich Burde, Karel Dekimpe

item.title: Yang-Baxter permutation group actions on distributive Yang-Baxter algebras
item.description: arXiv:2609.14220v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $(X,r)$ be a finite square-free distributive set-theoretic solution of the Yang-Baxter equation, and let $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ be its associated Yang-Baxter algebra. We prove that $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ is isomorphic to a skew polynomial algebra and explicitly compute its Nakayama automorphism. We study the natural faithful action of the permutation group $\mathcal{G}(X,r)$ on $\mathcal{A}(X,r)$ by graded algebra automorphisms. We characterize when $\mathcal{G}(X,r)$ is a reflection group and, in that case, describe the invariant subalgebra $\mathcal{A}(X,r)^{\mathcal{G}(X,r)}$ together with its Jacobian, reflection arrangement, and discriminant. We further establish a necessary and sufficient condition for the noncommutative Auslander theorem to hold for the permutation group action on a distributive Yang-Baxter algebra. Finally, for a class of non-trivial distributive Yang-Baxter algebras, we obtain a lower bound for the pertinency of the permutation group action.
item.dc:creator: Ji-Wei He, Xiaolan Yu

item.title: The algebraic and geometric classification of $3$-Poisson algebras
item.description: arXiv:2610.27300v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: $3$-Poisson (ternary Nambu--Poisson) algebras are the algebras of observables of Nambu mechanics, the generalization of Hamiltonian mechanics in which the time evolution $\dot f=\{f,H_1,H_2\}$ is governed by two Hamiltonians and preserves the phase volume; their $3$-Lie part also gives the gauge algebra of the Bagger--Lambert--Gustavsson model of multiple M2-branes. We give the algebraic classification of complex $4$-dimensional $3$-Poisson algebras (seven algebras) and of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent $3$-Poisson algebras ($38$ algebras and one one-parameter family) with both multiplications non-zero. We also describe the algebraic counterpart of the In\"on\"u--Wigner contractions of physics: the variety of complex $4$-dimensional $3$-Poisson algebras has dimension $16$ and seven irreducible components, one of which is the orbit closure of the simple $3$-Lie algebra of the M2-brane model, and the variety of complex $5$-dimensional nilpotent $3$-Poisson algebras has dimension $20$ and five irreducible components.
item.dc:creator: Hani Abdelwahab, Kobiljon Abdurasulov, Ivan Kaygorodov

item.title: A general paracontrolled ansatz for singular SPDEs
item.description: arXiv:2608.09700v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We provide a general ansatz for the paracontrolled approach introduced by Gubinelli, Imkeller, Perkowski for treating singular SPDEs. The ansatz proposed covers a large class of equations. It is described via decorated trees that encode its coefficients and its stochastic data. The main novelty is the recursive definition of the paracontrolled stochastic iterated integrals that involve a well-chosen combinatorial set of words. The paralinearisation is performed via a lift of iterated paraproducts to modelled distributions. The main idea is to integrate localised iterated paraproducts in order to get a global object with a good regularity. We also provide a fixed point argument and the renormalised equation with this ansatz when one uses the preparation map formalism that encompasses the BPHZ renormalisation. The last main result is the convergence of the renormalised stochastic data via the BPHZ renormalisation using an adaptation of the spectral gap approach. One obtains in the end a general solution theory for parabolic singular SPDEs via the paracontrolled approach.
item.dc:creator: Yvain Bruned, Nicolas Moench

item.title: Weighted Power Means on Upper Triangular Matrix Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.24821v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study weighted power means on the Lie group $\operatorname{UT}_n$ of real upper triangular matrices with positive diagonal entries. For $t\in\mathbb R\setminus\{0\}$, the weighted power mean $P_t(\mathbf{w}; A_1,\ldots,A_m)$ is defined by \[ X=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i(X\#_tA_i), \qquad X\#_tA:=X(X^{-1}A)^t. \] Using divided differences, analytic matrix functions, and the Parlett recurrence, we prove existence, uniqueness, and real-analytic dependence of $P_t$ on the data and the weights. We derive finite entrywise and block-recursive algorithms, establish structural properties of the mean, and obtain explicit formulas for the cases $\operatorname{UT}_2$ and $\operatorname{UT}_3$. We prove that $P_t$ converges to the weighted Karcher mean as $t\to 0$. We also establish a Lie--Trotter formula and derive second-order asymptotic expansions for the power, Karcher, and log-Euclidean means, showing that the parameter $t$ first enters the local behavior at second order.
item.dc:creator: Huajun Huang, Jimmie Lawson
